subject: Encryption ownership & logging confirmation for PayCore POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@paycore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: encryption ownership & logging asks

Hi Aisha / PayCore security team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — good conversation. Per our call I wanted to summarize the open items on encryption and logging so we can scope the POC and the technical workshop:

1) Encryption in transit: confirmation that TLS 1.2+ with mutual TLS for our private endpoints meets your requirement. Please confirm if you need client cert rotation cadence documented.
2) Encryption at rest: two high-level options discussed — Redwood-managed keys (RKM) vs customer-managed keys (BYOK). We captured PayCore's preference for BYOK but wanted the specific constraints below.
3) BYOK specifics: cloud KMS vs HSM-backed keys, key rotation policy, ability to revoke/rotate without data loss, and whether you require split custody/escrow.
4) Audit logging: required retention window (you mentioned 1 year as preferred, please confirm), sampling vs full logging, and fields you need in logs (token IDs, request metadata, partial prompt hashes, not full user content).
5) PII handling: categories of data you deem PII in the test prompts (cardholder name, PAN last4, full PAN), and whether you want automatic redaction at the prefix layer or post-response redaction.

Attachments: I attached the redwood-byo-key-runbook and the standard PO questions spreadsheet to help you fill in any constraints.

Next steps suggested:
- A short technical workshop (1 hour) with your infra/security + our crypto/ops team — proposed times in the related HubSpot note.
- If BYOK is required, we will prepare a KMS integration checklist (cloud providers + HSM vendor options).

Can you confirm: 1) target retention for audit logs, 2) BYOK vs Redwood-managed preference, and 3) whether your legal team needs key escrow language up front?

Thanks,

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@paycore.com>

Cc: security@paycore.com
Date: 2028-05-18T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: encryption ownership & logging asks

Jordan —

Great recap, thanks. Quick answers below to unblock scheduling: 

1) TLS: TLS 1.2 is acceptable for the demo but for production we require TLS 1.3 + mTLS for any private VPC endpoints. Rotation cadence: annual or on-compromise — we can accept your documented process.
2) BYOK: PayCore prefers BYOK with cloud KMS for the POC (we use AWS KMS), but product requires us to evaluate HSM-backed (CloudHSM) for keys that encrypt token caches.
3) Key rotation: rotation without re-encrypting stored embeddings is preferred — we need a description of your key-wrapping approach.
4) Audit logging: target retention 365 days, but we need the ability to export logs to our Splunk instance. Full request metadata required; content payload should be redacted/pseudonymized.
5) PII: treat full PAN and SSNs as sensitive — we will provide a sample set marking which prompt fields to consider PII.

I attached our internal KMS policy excerpt (paycore_kms_policy_v1.pdf). Please loop in your solutions team for the workshop.

Thanks,
Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Security Engineering | PayCore Payments
aisha.k@paycore.com

Attachments: paycore_kms_policy_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@paycore.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-18T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: encryption ownership & logging asks

Thanks Aisha — good clarifications. Adding a few technical notes so the workshop can be narrow and actionable: 

- TLS / mTLS: Redwood supports TLS 1.3 for hosted and private endpoints; we can enable client cert validation for dedicated/private deployments. We'll provide the cert rotation steps and automation hooks (ACME or internal cert manager).

- BYOK / Key wrapping: For the POC we offer two integration patterns: 
  a) Envelope encryption with customer KMS (recommended): data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant and wrapped with the customer KMS CMK. Rotating the CMK rotates the wrapping key but does not require full re-encryption of DEKs stored in our KV cache — we keep DEK versions and support key rollover.
  b) HSM-backed master key: if you need CloudHSM, we can integrate via an HSM-backed CMK; note additional latency on initial unwrapping.

- Rotation / Revocation: We support planned rotation and emergency revoke workflows; we log key-unwrap attempts and can include key version in audit events so you can trace usage back to a specific CMK version.

- Logging / retention: We can stream audit events to your Splunk via HTTPS/Syslog connector. Retention at Redwood side is configurable (30/90/365/retained-indefinitely for enterprise). For the POC we'll set 365 days and provide a retention export. Payloads will be redacted by default; we can pseudonymize with reversible tokens if required for debugging (with customer consent).

- PII handling: we recommend prefix redaction (on ingestion) for any prompt field flagged as sensitive; alternatively, we can ingest raw and apply post-response redaction — prefix redaction reduces exposure. We'll prepare a short matrix showing the tradeoffs for PayCore's flagged fields.

Proposed next step: 60-minute technical workshop this Thursday 2028-05-20 at 10:00 PT with PayCore infra/security + our crypto/ops (Marissa + Priyom). Jordan, can you confirm and send calendar invite?

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
